report.summary: Reviewed chunk 5 of correctness.py: _spawn_pytest, run_node_ids, TestRunner, validate_task. Verified docstring claims and code behavior.
risks: run_node_ids docstring | medium | Claims that fallback solo re-run is required because a single bad node aborts the whole batch even with --continue-on-collection-errors. This is an empirical claim about pytest behavior, not verifiable from code alone. | Test with pytest version to confirm.

run_node_ids | low | When all nodes unattributed and multiple nodes, solo re-runs each, but if solo also fails, status remains NOT_RUN. Could lead to silent failures. | Add logging or check for persistent NOT_RUN.
validate_task | low | Docstring says 'An EMPTY fail_to_pass is an error', but code only checks if field is missing; empty list passes validation. | Add check for empty fail_to_pass.

observations.what: In _spawn_pytest, if ManagedProcess is not None but CancellationUnavailable raised, proc remains None and falls back to subprocess.run.
In run_node_ids, when timed_out is True from batch, the function returns early without solo re-runs.
In run_node_ids, when len(unattributed) == len(nodes) == 1, it returns without solo re-run.
In run_node_ids, containment from solo runs overrides batch containment only if batch containment is 'none'.
validate_task docstring claims empty fail_to_pass is an error, but code only checks if field is present; empty list would pass.
